reviews.title: HOÀNG MINH ĐỨC · IELTS 49 · W07 · Đề 1
reviews.overall: Em viết đúng đề, đủ bốn đoạn và diễn đạt lại mở bài bằng “how many cars were made” phù hợp. Tuy nhiên, năm số em ghi khác bảng, trong đó số của Argentina năm 2003 lệch 60.000 xe. Overview nêu đúng Thailand dẫn đầu nhưng chưa nói nước này tăng tới đỉnh năm 2006 rồi giảm; từ “slightly” cũng làm nhẹ mức giảm hơn 162.000 xe. Cô yêu cầu em đối chiếu lại từng ô, sửa câu so sánh Argentina với Australia và bổ sung diễn biến của Thailand trước khi nộp lại.
reviews.dataGrouping: Em chia Detail 1 theo năm 2003 và 2006, rồi dùng Detail 2 cho năm 2009; cách chia này giúp thấy sự đổi hạng giữa Argentina và Australia. Hai đoạn đều có ít nhất hai câu và có so sánh. Khi sửa, em cần làm rõ giai đoạn 2006–2009 của Thailand và kiểm tra số liệu trước khi diễn giải mức tăng giảm.

reviews.originalEssay:
The table shows how many cars were made in Argentina, Australia, and Thailand in 2003, 2006, and 2009.
Overall, car production in Argentina and Thailand increased over the period, while the figure for Australia decreased. Additionally, Thailand produced the highest number of cars in all three years.
In 2003, Thailand was the leading car producer with 735,052 cars. Australia came second with 452,161 cars, while Argentina produced the lowest number at 295,088 cars. By 2006, the number of cars made in Thailand rose sharply to over 1.16 million. In contrast, Australia’s production dropped to 341,250 cars. Meanwhile, Argentina saw a moderate growth to 352,759 cars, which was higher than Australia.
In 2009, Thailand's production fell slightly to 999,910 cars but still remained the highest. Argentina continued to grow and reached its peak at 466,089 cars. On the other hand, the figure for Australia kept falling to a low of only 245,624 cars. As a result, Australia became the country with the lowest car production at the end of the period

reviews.suggestedRevision:
The table compares the numbers of cars manufactured in Argentina, Australia and Thailand in 2003, 2006 and 2009.

Overall, Argentina's car output rose steadily while Australia's declined throughout the period. Thailand remained the largest producer in every year; its output peaked in 2006 before falling, although the final figure was still above its 2003 level.

In 2003, Thailand made 735,852 cars, considerably more than Australia, at 452,163, and Argentina, at 235,088. By 2006, Thai production had risen sharply to 1,162,356 cars, reaching the highest figure in the table. Argentina's output also grew to 352,759, overtaking Australia's figure, which had fallen to 341,268.

Over the next three years, Thailand's output declined to 999,963 cars in 2009 but remained well ahead of the other two countries. Argentina continued to increase its production, reaching 466,089 cars at the end of the period. By contrast, the number made in Australia fell again to 245,624, leaving it with the lowest output in 2009. Compared with 2003, Argentina produced almost twice as many cars, whereas Australia's output was nearly halved.

Em viết đúng đề, đủ 167 từ, có bốn đoạn và so sánh đúng rằng số tù nhân nam luôn cao hơn nữ. Tuy nhiên, câu nói số nam giữ nguyên ở 20.000 từ sau 1931 đến 1971 trái với biểu đồ: số này phải tăng từ khoảng 10.000 lên gần 20.000. Đoạn nữ cũng kể giai đoạn sau 1941 như một đợt tăng liên tục, bỏ lần giảm từ 1961 đến 1971. Cô yêu cầu em sửa hai diễn biến này và nêu rõ bước tăng mạnh của nam trong 1971–1981; sau đó soát lại từ chỉ mức độ và dấu câu.

Overall, the male prison population increased significantly over the period, while the number of female prisoners experienced a decrease. Additionally, the number of male prisoners was always much higher than that of female prisoners in every year.

In contrast, the second graph shows that the female prison population began at about 3,200 in 1911. The figure then fell sharply to its lowest point of only 500 in 1941. From 1941 to 2001, the number of female prisoners recovered slightly and increased back to around 2,000 at the end of the period

Overall, male prisoners outnumbered female prisoners at every recorded point. The male prison population fell early on but then rose sharply, especially between 1971 and 1981. By contrast, the female figure dropped to a low in 1941, fluctuated afterwards and ended below its initial level.

The number of male prisoners was about 18,000 in both 1911 and 1921, before falling to roughly 10,000 in 1931. It then climbed to around 19,000 in 1951 and stayed close to 20,000 through 1971. A pronounced jump followed, taking the figure to approximately 39,000 in 1981, before it reached about 46,000 in 2001.

The female prison population started at approximately 3,200 in 1911 and declined to about 500 in 1941. It recovered to around 1,500 by 1961, but fell again to roughly 700 in 1971. Thereafter, it increased to about 1,900 in 2001, still well below its starting figure.

The line graph illustrates the proportion of female members of parliament in five European nations (Germany, Italy, France, the UK, and Belgium) from 2000 to 2012.
Overall, the percentage of female parliamentarians showed distinct upward trends in the UK, France, and Belgium, while Germany and Italy experienced overall net declines despite various fluctuations. Germany consistently maintained one of the highest figures throughout the majority of the twelve-year period.
In 2000, Germany recorded the highest percentage of female MPs at approximately 33%, peaking significantly at 37% in 2004 before dropping back down to around 32% by 2012. Conversely, Italy started at 27%, fluctuated slightly over the years, and ultimately fell to 23% in 2012, becoming the lowest among all five countries.
Meanwhile, the UK witnessed a steady rise from 23% in 2000 to 33% in 2012, eventually overtaking Germany. France and Belgium both experienced notable initial drops in 2004, down to 17% and 12% respectively. However, France saw a subsequent sharp surge to 31% by 2008 and remained stable, while Belgium rose remarkably to finish at 28%

The two pie charts compare the primary motivations driving students to choose a specific university in the United Kingdom in 1997 and 2007. 
Overall, the availability of suitable degree courses remained the single most important factor for students in both years. Furthermore, while the significance of proximity to the parental home and teaching quality grew noticeably over the ten-year period, the value placed on resources and extracurricular activities experienced a clear decline. 
In 1997, the leading reason was having suitable degree courses at 35%, which rose marginally to peak at 37% by 2007. Conversely, the percentage of students prioritizing good sports and social activities witnessed the sharpest drop, plummeting from 19% in 1997 to a mere 6% a decade later. Similarly, interest in the quality of resources fell from 21% to 17%. 
On the other hand, location became far more crucial, as the proportion for proximity to the parental home more than doubled from 10% to 22%, becoming the second highest reason. Meanwhile, the quality of teaching experienced a modest increase, rising slightly from 15% to 18% over the same timeframe
